## Update harnesses from the app

Nova Desktop 0.10.3 adds an Update action to the harness the Agents tab already reports as out of date: it runs that CLI's own updater from the app and shows what the CLI printed.

### Added

- Agents → Harnesses: expanding a harness that has a newer published version now offers `Update to <version>`. The button runs the harness's own updater — `nova update`, `pi update`, `claude update`, `codex update`, `opencode upgrade`, `commandcode cmd update`, `hermes update` — from the app's config directory, so nothing runs inside your workspace.
- The row then reports the version that `--version` prints afterwards, re-read against the registries, instead of trusting what the updater claimed.
- The updater's own stdout and stderr is shown under the row, so a failure explains itself rather than becoming a generic error.
- Only one updater runs at a time; every update button is disabled while one is in flight, because two package-manager runs in the same install tree corrupt it.

### Guardrails

- The update command line is a fixed table keyed by agent id in `src-tauri/src/agent/cli.rs`; the UI sends an id and never a command.
- A Nova running from a source checkout refuses to update itself, since `nova update` would fetch a second copy rather than move that one.
- Updaters run with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and `kill_on_drop`, time out after five minutes, and their combined output is clipped to 4000 characters.

### Validation

- New Rust test `updater_arguments_are_the_harness_own_commands` pins all seven argv tables and an unknown id.
- A real no-op run of `codex update` while already at its published version returned exit 0, printed its install log, and read back the same version — exercising the argv, output capture and version read-back end to end.
- `npm run lint`, the frontend suite (109 tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `npm run test:rust` (217 passed) all pass on this version.

### Not covered

- No automated check clicks the button: the repo has no jsdom or app-browser harness, so the command and the panel are covered by unit tests rather than a driven UI.
- A harness installed as a script shim (`pi.cmd`/`pi.ps1`) is not found by `resolve()`, so its row stays on "Not found" and never offers the button. That gap predates this release.
